statements.text: The UK will double down on support for Ukraine. The Prime Minister is set to tell President Zelenskyy that he has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military support and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks, and to accelerate delivery of critical air defence missiles.

The Prime Minister welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire. President Zelenskyy has assured him that Ukraine would immediately implement it once a start date is confirmed, and the Prime Minister will discuss this further with President Zelenskyy in the coming days.

The UK's assessment is that the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard. The UK will bring further sanctions to restrict the capacity of Iran and the IRGC to do it harm.

The UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. A trade deal on food and drink products is on the table, which the Prime Minister said is expected to add the equivalent of over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040.
Britain has decided to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia to provide air-to-air refuelling support. A Voyager aircraft has already completed 14 operational missions.

Chancellor Merz and the Prime Minister agreed a new partnership in Berlin to tackle Russia's hybrid threats. The UK has confirmed its commitment to establish a new National Centre for Information Defence, as recommended by the Foreign Affairs Select Committee.

The Prime Minister raised the Falkland Islands and the clear and declared will of the islanders to remain British with President Trump, and said the UK will always do whatever it takes to uphold the islanders' will.

The UK will accelerate deliveries of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. The UK has already committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of them to Ukraine over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of the £45 million package announced today to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter requirements.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: The UK is standing by plans to fully implement a maritime services ban on Russian LNG exports. Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey urged partners to back the ban, like the UK has done, to curtail the war chest funding Putin.

At the meeting in Downing Street, the leaders underlined that Russia had no interest in peace. They discussed how the UK could accelerate defensive support to Ukraine ahead of the winter, including long range missiles.

Becketwell in Derby has been chosen as the site of the Great British Railways headquarters. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029, with an estimated £151 million boost to the Derby economy and up to 450 GBR staff.
Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway, and that she is delighted Becketwell will become GBR's new home.

Andy Burnham said he is making an offer to the Scottish Government. Douglas Alexander said the offer is a genuine one and that the Scotland Office is ready to work alongside the Scottish Government to make it happen.

The Prime Minister is offering Scotland DWP devolution, a model of localised employment support shaped by Holyrood. The National Economic Council is due to meet in a couple of weeks with the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland to put the offer on the table.
The Scottish Government has agreed to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west.

Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship, with the first starters based in Derby. Pat McFadden said this forms part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities for young people to earn or learn.
